methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict winning with 54 series units?
How should adherence be measured and validated without outcome-derived labels or lookahead leakage?
What power, exposure, confounding, and data-version constraints apply on 2026-06-16, when the 2025-26 playoff data are still partial?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 (p=0.008) was inflated by n and team-quality confounding. Series-level rho=-0.26 (p=0.07, n=50) was underpowered; the record states ~80 series are needed for p<0.05. Low AVOID-share bin 52.6% vs 25-50% bin 37.0%. Verdict recorded as inconclusive; validation not recorded.

Audit of an LLM adaptation-analysis batch claiming 'adaptation predicts series winners 9/10'. Recorded problems: 706 findings with n<5; series winners never looked up (0/2073 calls); winners LLM-inferred; a score invented; point costs from LLM arithmetic.

Execution conformance of observed play mix vs recommended opener: average |delta| 4.5 to 24.0 pp across leverage buckets; 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. Single 2025-26 playoff G1s, about 100 possessions per game, no outcome comparison; CUT and PNR muted by tagger floor.

Ranked playsheet validation over 10 series: Spearman rho=-0.0639 (p=0.0997, n=665), no full-rank signal. Kruskal-Wallis H=32.97 (p=2.7e-05). Mann-Whitney BEST 1.257 (n=56) vs AVOID 1.092 (n=160), p=0.004. Trigger accuracy rho=0.4525 (n=121).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing series-level AVOID share as a predictor of winning without controlling for team quality.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as underpowered (n=50, p=0.07; ~80 needed) and confounded by team quality (the record cites OKC as disciplined and good). The game-level result was inflated by non-independent observations.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Batch analysis of adaptation claims, including a '9/10 adaptation predicts winning' rule.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact: winners were inferred rather than looked up, findings had n<5, and numbers were LLM-generated, so the apparent effect was produced by construction and labelling flaws.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring conformance of observed mix to the recommended mix as a basis for an outcome claim.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as mechanism unclear. Single-game horizon, no outcome comparison, and tagger floor muted some play types, so conformance was descriptive only.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranked playsheet counter prediction of which alternative scored better.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a null full-rank signal (Spearman p=0.10). The pairwise BEST>AVOID result rested on small samples and was limited by leakage, measurement reliability, and small sample size.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project on closely related counter-strategy questions (SF-CHT-039, SF-APPS-018) found no adequately powered evidence that play-mix or playsheet adherence predicts winning.
Series-level tests with about 50 units were recorded as underpowered, and the record puts the requirement near 80 series for the related correlation.
Team-quality confounding was recorded as a live threat to any mix-to-winning association.
Adherence measurement has been recorded as unreliable at the play-type level (SF-APPS-017), and the one validation attempt was not recorded.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests the stated question directly: adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix versus winning.
No record shows a validated adherence metric, a validated suppression-conditional recommendation, or a pre-specified test.
No record establishes a sample size or effect size adequate for 54 series, and none gives a power calculation for this specific question.
The retrieved records do not show whether the 2025-26 playoff data are complete for the analysis date.
own_inferences: With 54 series and a likely small effect, the test is probably underpowered, as SF-CHT-039 was at 50 series.
Adherence is probably correlated with team quality and playoff-round context, so a raw adherence-to-winning association would be confounded.
The 2025-26 playoff data were partial on 2026-06-16 and will be complete only from 2026-06-21, so using them now would mix data versions.
Game-level analyses would inflate the effective n because games within a series are not independent.
uncertainties: The records do not show the exact definition of the suppression-conditional recommended mix or how it was derived.
It is unknown whether the recommendation was built from outcome data, which would create label leakage.
The effect size of adherence on winning is unknown; the retrieved records give no estimate for this question.
Whether the 2025-26 playoff series count within the 54 units is final is not confirmed.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that closely related series-level tests (SF-CHT-039, SF-APPS-018) were underpowered, confounded, or null, and that a similar batch-analysis claim was an artifact (SF-APPA-008). This moved the decision from a plain proceed to do_not_proceed as posed, with a minimum viable test specified below. No record tests the exact question, so the decision rests on these related findings and on the stated sample size.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series is below the roughly 80 series the SF-CHT-039 record cites for its related correlation at p<0.05, and the expected effect size is unknown.
Team quality and round context are likely to drive both adherence and winning; no record shows a valid control.
Play-type tagging has a recorded floor (SF-APPS-017), and adherence is not validated.
If the recommended mix was built from the same outcomes, adherence scores are not independent of winning (SF-APPA-008 shows this failure mode).
Seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26 may differ in play-type mix and suppression; the 2025-26 playoffs were partial on the analysis date.

prior_work.summary: Related earlier studies (SF-CHT-039, SF-APPS-018) tested series-level counter-strategy measures against winning and found weak, underpowered, or confounded results. SF-APPS-017 measured mix conformance descriptively with no outcome test. SF-APPA-008 is an artifact. None tests adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix against winning directly, so the question is only partly addressed.

risks.text: 54 series units is likely insufficient for a modest adherence-to-winning effect; SF-CHT-039 needed about 80 series for p<0.05 on a related test.
Team quality, seed, and opponent strength are likely to drive both mix adherence and winning, as SF-CHT-039 noted.
Adherence depends on play-type tagging with a recorded floor (SF-APPS-017); the SF-APPS-018 trigger signal rested on small n.
If the recommended mix or suppression condition uses playoff outcomes, adherence is circular with the target.
SF-APPS-018 was limited by leakage; any use of future possessions to define adherence or the recommendation would bias results.
Some play types and matchup pairs occur rarely per series, so per-series adherence estimates are noisy.
Season-to-season change and partial 2025-26 playoff data as of 2026-06-16 can mix data versions.
Several mix definitions, leverage buckets, and round splits would inflate false positives unless fixed in advance.
No placebo or negative-control adherence measure is recorded; a placebo would be needed to rule out artifacts like SF-APPA-008.

design.estimand: Association between a pre-registered adherence index to a suppression-conditional recommended mix and the probability of winning a playoff series, adjusted for team quality, seed, and round. This is a pre-registration-quality target; it is not supported by the retrieved records.
design.unit: Playoff series (one row per series), with game-level data used only for descriptive checks.
design.sample: Only completed series from 2022-23 to 2024-25 (approximately 54 units or fewer). 2025-26 playoff data are excluded until complete (from 2026-06-21) to avoid mixing data versions.
design.power: Before analysis, compute the detectable effect for 54 series. The SF-CHT-039 record implies that about 80 series are needed for a comparable correlation at p<0.05. With roughly 54 series, the minimum viable test is only powered for a large effect, so report the minimum detectable effect and do not claim a null from an underpowered test.
design.controls: Adjust for team strength (pre-series rating), seed, home-court, and round. Define the adherence index from pre-series or pre-game information only, with no future possessions and no playoff outcomes. Validate play-type tagging reliability before use. Use a placebo adherence measure (for example, a mix from a non-suppressed condition) as a negative control.
design.falsification: Pre-register that the association must survive team-quality adjustment and hold in a placebo adherence measure. If the adjusted effect is not distinguishable from the placebo, reject the claim. If the placebo shows a similar association, treat the result as an artifact.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary adherence definition and one primary test. Apply correction for any secondary definitions, leverage buckets, or round splits.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if the adherence index is validated (reliability reported), the adjusted effect with a confidence interval excludes zero, and the placebo measure shows no comparable association. Otherwise report the result as inconclusive or untestable at this sample size.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Freeze the version before analysis. Exclude 2025-26 playoff data until complete on 2026-06-21.

methodological_questions: Can adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series or game winning with 54 series units?
How should adherence be measured and validated against outcomes without outcome-derived labels or lookahead leakage?
What sample size, exposure sparsity, and confounding risks apply to testing a mix-adherence predictor of winning?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series
